business_rules.statement: The platform is provisioned with exactly one Super Admin account, created through the backend at platform commissioning and never through any user interface.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Backend commissioning; no user interface path exists

business_rules.statement: Exactly one root account exists, and no user interface path creates a second.
Roles are fixed at V1 with no custom role authoring; custom roles are roadmap.
A Platform Engineer's change is submitted and takes effect only when an Admin approves it (maker-checker).
No account can approve its own submission.
All ten critical-class actions route to the root, and an Admin cannot approve any of them.
Approval requests carry all nine stated fields and commit under the one-transaction guarantee.
A pending change renders as pending on the target object as well as in the queue; nothing applies silently.
Composed-agent reviews and tier publications appear in the same queue under their own classes, and no parallel decision queue exists.
The implementation authoring role can author and submit inside a tenant workspace but can never approve or release, and its provisioning and revocation appear in both audit streams.
The live per-module roles matrix contains no blank cell — every cell carries an explicit status from the closed set.
The create control is visible only to the root and absent for everyone else, rather than present and disabled.
business_rules.applies_to: Account creation, role assignment, disable controls

business_rules.statement: Console has no offline mode; no approval is cached or applied from a stale client, which is a segregation-of-duties control as much as a technical one.

An approved change destined for a device becomes a command and waits; the queue shows the change applied at the platform and the fleet view shows the command's exact state at each device — two deliberately different facts, never conflated.
No public self-signup path exists; every tenant is created by the client's platform team. Onboarding is invitation-driven.
Tenant creation provisions an isolated data space, and isolation is architectural rather than a permission setting.
Soft suspension blocks master-data writes while runs continue to be created, scheduled, and executed.
Under soft suspension, only the Tenant Admin sees a banner; no other tenant user sees any indication.
Hard suspension permits the enumerated completion pipeline and blocks all new runs.
Compliance suspension blocks all logins immediately, stops in-flight runs, and locks devices at next contact with the fixed message.
The only platform-side entry into a compliance-suspended tenant is the dual-authorised compliance-emergency path.
A device lock is never rendered as applied before the device acknowledges it.
Pilot conversion preserves the tenant identifier and requires no re-onboarding.
Downgrades never execute mid-cycle and carry a visible pending-downgrade status, queued behind consumption fit.
Tenant groups have no operational behaviour and are never visible in any tenant surface.
No operational action of any kind can be taken from the tenant detail page by any console role — visibility, not intervention.
The worker-facing compliance message is fixed: "Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved."
business_rules.enforcement_point: Frontline Worker Application device string (ships with the application)

business_rules.statement: No measure exposes operational content, and the boundary is enforced in the pipeline rather than in the user interface.
Comparative views are anonymised before aggregation and cannot be de-anonymised by any account including the root.
Override audit is queryable for frequency and clustering and never returns record contents.
A zero is never rendered for a missing measure; the measure degrades stale-with-age, then narrowed, then unavailable.
Tier records carry all six field groups and no price metadata; the platform does not price or bill.
Tier publication is critical-class and cannot be performed by an Admin alone.
Grandfathering treatment is mandatory in the change record before submission.
Per-tenant overrides are flags on the tenant record and never edits to the tier.
Agent Author gates Growth and Enterprise; Job Type and Service Type are ungated.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Studio Agent Builder gating from the tier record

business_rules.statement: No invoicing, payment execution, or pricing capability exists anywhere on the platform.
No ladder threshold blocks work; the strongest outcome is a flag.
Burst entry is recorded as its own event.
Late-arriving events are attributed to their event time, not their arrival time.
A metering change is reprocessing, not data loss: the ledger is event-sourced and reconstructable end to end.
No console role can enroll a tenant's device; enrollment is tenant-self-service within platform policy.
Wipe and de-authorisation are critical-class and mirrored to the tenant's audit stream.
Every erasure on a reachable device is preceded by a final sync attempt of pending captures — de-authorising a device must not destroy unsynced work.
No console view renders an unreached device as wiped, locked, or updated.
The per-device package inventory records which package version each run executed against.

The cache-validity rule bounds how long cached credentials and suspension states are trusted on an offline device before forced re-sync — the control that stops a suspended worker continuing on a dark tablet.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Device-side cache-validity enforcement, bounded by the floor register

business_rules.statement: Exactly two channels exist — in-app and email — and no configuration adds a third.
In-app banners cannot be muted by any tenant user.
All-tenant broadcasts require root approval (critical class); single-tenant notices do not.
Every send stores an audience snapshot taken at send time.
Delivery, opening, and acknowledgement are tracked as distinct states and never conflated.
A re-send after partial failure uses the stored snapshot rather than a fresh one.
None of the notifications enforces the suspension; the suspension is enforced by the authorisation layer and, on devices, by the applied command.
No write capability exists inside a normal support session for any account including the root — read-only without exception.
A session cannot open without a ticket-linked reason class.
Sessions expire at their time box, default two hours, and cannot be extended in place.
A persistent banner naming the engineer and start time renders to the tenant for the whole session, with a working End-session control.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Tenant UI rendering property (not the notification machinery)

business_rules.statement: Pressing End session terminates platform access immediately.
The compliance-emergency path requires a named emergency class and two authorisations and cannot be initiated by one person.
The emergency session's scope is declared before it opens and cannot be widened during it.
The compliance-emergency path is the only write path into tenant data and the only entry into a compliance-suspended tenant.
No ambient browsing capability exists anywhere on the console.
Where the banner cannot render, the session does not open. A notification may never be the only mechanism disclosing a platform-side access.
JBS holds no standing access; no default grant exists in any environment.
Every grant enumerates its scope, carries a time box, and links a reason before it can be submitted.
Custody of the root account rests with the client and JBS cannot hold it.
No purge capability exists anywhere on the platform for any account; nothing ages out of existence.
The retention value is a hot-retrievability horizon and shortening it moves data rather than deleting it.
A legal hold suspends tiering and compliance-driven deletion for its scope, and place and release are both dual-approved and tenant-visible.
Anonymisation runs at 24 months for standard commercial tenants and never in Regulated-Industry mode.
Anonymisation preserves the measurement, the result, and the evidence and replaces only the identity.
Anonymisation cannot be reversed by any account, and switching into Regulated-Industry mode later does not resurrect identities.
Upcoming anonymisation events are surfaced before they execute.
Offboarding executes export-on-archival at no charge before archival.
The erasure workflow cannot skip the legal-hold check and always writes a certificate to both audit trails.
No code path exists where an administrative change commits and its audit event does not — the one-transaction guarantee, rendered ENFORCED.
An audit-write failure refuses the action and the operator is told — an action that cannot be audited does not happen.
No edit or delete path exists on any surface for any account.
Every cross-tenant access event mirrors into the affected tenant's audit stream.
Platform Access History reads the same records rather than a separate view.
Audit retention is never shorter than the tenant data it evidences.
business_rules.enforcement_point: FB-SA-10 at the point of configuration

business_rules.statement: Tamper-evidence by chained hashes is rendered as a V2 hardening and is not claimed at V1.
Every write path, tenant-side and platform-side, lands at the registry, and no bypass exists.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected at the point of entry with the bound stated and is not stored — never accepted and logged.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Registry bound validation against the platform floor register

business_rules.statement: All seventeen governed settings are present and each has a floor-register bound.
Current-value changes platform-side are Admin actions, default changes are engineering-class, and bound changes are critical-class.
Tightening a bound surfaces non-conforming values rather than rewriting them.
A global disable cannot be re-enabled by any tier, entitlement, override, cohort, or tenant value — a global disable is a ceiling.
The fourteen-step evaluation order is fixed and not configurable.
A control cannot be submitted unless its blast-radius preview asserts that no Severity 1 path, specification gate, evaluation gate, or on-device deterministic behaviour is touched.
The D6 disabled semantic (Unavailable and unexplained) is not selectable.
Controls below tenant scope cannot be created; Site, Area, Location, Job and worker scopes are deliberately excluded.
No Boolean blocked field exists on the tenant record; blocking is expressed through the three defined suspension states.
A release supersedes a queued, unapplied suspension via fencing token, and the superseded command's state is recorded rather than discarded.
No taxonomy entry with a non-zero reference count can be hard-deleted by any account.

business_rules.statement: A catalog write with an incomplete locale fails rather than shipping a gap (English and Spanish both required).
business_rules.applies_to: Job Type and Service Type records

business_rules.statement: Both platform-seeded catalogues are empty at version 1, and loading client-supplied entries later leaves every tenant-created entry unchanged in name, code, identifier and reference count.
business_rules.applies_to: Job Type and Service Type catalogs

business_rules.statement: Every one of the sixteen prohibited acts is unavailable to all four console roles including the root.

A count that the Statement of Work states is quoted, never recomputed; a count it does not state is derived, labelled derived, and carries the decision identifier recording the gap; an arbitrary count is a defect.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Chapter 24 inventory authoring and traceability checks

business_rules.statement: No row carries an empty cell. Cells that do not apply carry `Not applicable` with a stated reason.
A row that would change a number the Statement of Work states cannot be published by an author; it becomes a scope decision with a DEC identifier.
Identifiers are never silently reused; removal leaves a retired-identifier record, because a reused identifier corrupts every historical acceptance record that referenced it.
At module level the inventory is exhaustive; at feature level exhaustive against cited source sections; at sub-feature and function level it is representative and stated as such.
The operational action set contains exactly ten entries and no eleventh action exists anywhere in the delivered surface.
business_rules.enforcement_point: TEST-CC-INV-001 against the delivered action registry

business_rules.statement: The Read-only Auditor cannot authenticate into the Client Command Center at all, and the attempt is audited.
No pace state, flag, or timer derived from pace is transmitted to any Frontline device.
Every Band A safety row is Offline-capable — executes on device, with no safety behaviour depending on connectivity.
No row and no delivered screen exposes a pace figure, timer against expectation, or comparison to other workers.
No console view reaches record-level operational content outside one of the three named access classes.
None of the six enforced invariants has an off control, an approval path, or a configuration key on any screen, for any account including the root.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A derived view or telemetry measure degrades or its source is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Render stale-with-age, then per-tenant primaries without roll-up, then "measure unavailable"
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where anonymisation cannot be guaranteed for a comparative view, the view renders unavailable rather than degrading to named data
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An unavailable measure; a zero is never rendered for a missing measure
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Recompute over the gap window and record the degraded window; reconcile recomputed against previously reported figures

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An approval cannot apply or commit
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry with the same idempotency key, then hold the request at pending and surface the failure to the approver
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: FB-SA-04 where the consequence is device-bound
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The target object unchanged with the request visibly waiting; the prior value or version stays in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-drive from the pending record; reconciliation compares the applied value against the request diff

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An audit write or tenant-audit mirroring cannot commit
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the whole transaction once, then refuse the action entirely
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: n/a — refusal is the design; there is no queued-audit path and no client-side buffer
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Nothing changed and the operator is told the action was refused and why
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-drive from the operator's intent, never from a buffered audit entry

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A command (suspension, lock, wipe, package distribution) cannot reach its device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Keep the command queued, retry on the device's own schedule, escalate to the platform team with the command's exact state named
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device remains unreached; DEC-WIPE-001 governs the unresolved lifetime
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform-side block fully in force while the device remains unlocked and unreachable, rendered honestly
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Commands apply in order with fencing tokens on reconnection; superseded commands are rejected and recorded as `superseded`

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Session machinery fails mid-session
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Terminate the session immediately and hold the tenant banner until closure is confirmed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the underlying grant cannot be revoked, revoke the console account's session entirely
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A closed session with no write capability ever having existed, banner cleared only on confirmed closure
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A new session with a new reason is required; no resumption

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A notification, banner or post-session report cannot be delivered (email vendor failure)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Keep the unmutable in-app banner present, retry email, record per-recipient failure
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No second vendor exists; escalate to the platform team with the failed recipient list
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: In-app-only delivery with recorded email failures; the queue itself remains the enforcing mechanism
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-send against the stored audience snapshot rather than a fresh one; the report is retained regardless

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A scheduler or scheduled export misfires
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-run on detection, then backfill the missed window under supervision, with the misfire recorded with its window
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: For exports, regenerate the whole extract rather than patching a partial one
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: For tiering, data stays hot — costs money, loses nothing; for grants, manual revocation rather than trusting the scheduler
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-drive each scheduler; the anonymisation backfill must be idempotent and must verify before acting

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Total console unavailability
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: No approvals apply; tenants are unaffected
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: n/a
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Administrative intent is replayed rather than auto-applied on recovery
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Replay administrative intent after recovery

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Bound validation against the platform floor register is unavailable, or a policy change cannot validate
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry, then reject the write with the bound stated
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: n/a — rejection is the behaviour, not the failure
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The existing value unchanged; accepting an unvalidated value would breach the configurability principle at its one enforcement point
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-drive the write; a per-tenant conformance report surfaces non-conforming values rather than rewriting them

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Failure in the on-device deterministic safety layer: gates, specification checks, severity classification, the immediate Severity 1 hold
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Controlled block
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No off switch exists
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A controlled block, never a bypass
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Owned by Chapter 38, Universal Fallback Architecture

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Upload queue, command channel, dual timestamps, clock-skew guard or version pinning failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Durable queue and resumable upload; commands applied in order at next sync
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Owned by Chapter 38
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Evidence held in the encrypted store; media evicted only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Queue drain in server-receipt order, command application in order, hold propagation, conflict review

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Artificial intelligence degraded or unavailable, including the platform emergency pause

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Owned by Chapter 38

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An approval-chain or maker-checker participant is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Owned by Chapter 38, without ever collapsing segregation of duties
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Release Authority absence is Not specified in the Statement of Work; a standing deputy Release Authority is Recommendation — R&D
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The prior published version stays in force and the floor keeps running on it, safe because version pinning means no in-flight run is affected

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The feature-control evaluation service is unavailable so effective values cannot be computed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Serve the last computed effective value with its age, for a bounded period
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Fall back to the most restrictive value consistent with the platform invariants — invariants remain on, everything else evaluates to disabled
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A platform on which enforced invariants hold, no optional capability is available, and every surface says so
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Recompute on restoration; a per-tenant effective-value report compares computed against served values with divergence raised as an audit finding

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A legal hold cannot be placed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Immediate escalation rather than a silent retry — the gravest case in MOD-SA-17
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Unprotected data may tier or be deleted while the failure is unnoticed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Tiering for the intended scope is suspended by a broader manual hold until the precise one can be placed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Place the precise hold and release the broader manual suspension

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The built system and Chapter 24 diverge
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A reconciliation pass that adds the missing rows with their classification
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A delivered capability has no source and no decision identifier
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The capability is disabled behind its feature switch until a decision identifier is issued and accepted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Issue the decision, add the row, re-run the traceability check, republish with a version bump and change note
